medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
Penn State College of Medicine's Cognitive Skills Program (CSP) provides comprehensive cognitive skills development and learning support to our medical, graduate, and physician assistant students.

The CSP offers workshops, interactive learning sessions, and individual support for exploring content, processes, and thinking skills to maximize our students' success. The CSP serves all students in the College of Medicine by providing programs to help promote effective and efficient life-long learning. The CSP also provides remediation services for students who are struggling academically. 

For more information, please visit https://med.psu.edu/education/academic-resources/cognitive-skills-program.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Leaves of absence are granted on a case by case basis for personal or academic reasons.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
The Societies Program supports all the educational opportunities of our students. Each student is assigned to one of five societies. Our fifth society represents the students at the University Park Regional Campus. The Societies provide a personalized longitudinal four-year structure for clinical skills, clinical reasoning and wellness development, academic advising, and professional and personal coaching. Students are supported by both Academic Counseling and Specialty Career Advising. The Societies Program also aims to foster camaraderie between students and faculty offering a variety of social events.

The Office of Student Affairs aims to support students in all aspects of student life beyond academics. Community service and interest group organizations allow students ample opportunity to explore interests. Programming also attends to student wellness and celebrates all student milestones
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
Hershey Site
This 550-acre campus is located near the state capital of Harrisburg. It houses the College of Medicine, a 600+ bed University Hospital and Children’s Hospital, Emergency Medicine/Trauma Center, Cancer Institute, Women’s Health Center, and Biomedical Research Building. The Hospital is the only regional Level 1 Trauma Center for both adult and pediatric cases. The medical campus has a Fitness Center, student housing, and outdoor recreational facilities. The area offers an array of arts, music, sports, dining, and outdoor recreational opportunities.

University Park Site
The Mount Nittany Medical Center is a full service 260 bed facility. It is adjacent to the Penn State Main Campus with 45,000 students and will allow interaction with a number of health-related colleges in addition to the law and business schools.  Medical students have access to sports and recreational events in the setting of a college town.
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
The Hershey campus offers on-campus housing that is utilized by the majority of medical students.  The University Manor complex is a safe environment with affordable apartments situated on campus with numerous amenities.  In addition, a large apartment complex is located within a 5-10 minute walk from the medical campus.  See the College of Medicine website for detailed information. 

The University Park campus has apartment housing available near the Medical Center that is utilized by the majority of students.  See the Program website for detailed information.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The Office of Health Advancement and Community Engagement supports a student group that is focused on topics and concerns of the gender and sexual minority community to provide a place for community and support. The Office for a Respectful Learning Environment ensures that there are avenues to address any challenges and concerns within the learning environment. Trainings are provided to faculty, staff and students regarding issues that are faced by individuals and communities that identify as LGBTQIA+, highlighting practices that foster inclusion and equity.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Penn State College of Medicine is committed to the success of students with disabilities in all its academic programs. Students with disabilities may be able to receive reasonable accommodations to eliminate barriers to success. For more information, please visit https://med.psu.edu/about/health-advancement-community-engagement/student-disability-services.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Penn State College of Medicine provides various wellness opportunities and resources that touch on the 8 Dimensions of Wellness. The University Fitness Center, Financial Aid and the Professional Mental Health offices are available to support students with their health focus. The Office of Student Affairs collaborates with the Student Wellness Committee on providing additional events throughout the year to engage with students.

In addition, there is a dedicated Wellness Day each semester. On these days, classes are dismissed and a variety of activities are available for students on campus that include physical, nutritional, mental and social wellness activities.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
Our culture is inviting and collaborative, where students feel supported and encouraged. Student clubs, campus events and community outreach programs cater to students' interests while building lasting friendships. Faculty and staff mentor and take time to engage with students, fostering a strong sense of belonging. Partnering with a world-class multi-hospital health system provides easy access to both shadowing and research. This supportive atmosphere enhances learning and encourages innovation and research.
 
State College offers a supportive environment for medical education. It offers unique access to faculty, programming and resources of Penn State University. The small class size (12 students per year) at University Park fosters a close-knit learning community with personalized attention and support from faculty and peers. This remarkable learning environment promotes critical thinking, teamwork and a collaborative approach to medical education and clinical care.

medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students begin patient interactions in the fall of first year as part of a robust patient experience and health systems science curriculum and clinical skills course.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Students engage in two common instructional formats – small-group problem-based learning and direct patient experiences – with variations on the intensity with which each is used.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Core clinical rotations begins in January of the second year and extends for fourteen months. Sites include urban locations, academic referral centers, and community hospitals.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Large lectures are video-taped and attendance is not required.  Students are reminded of the opportunity to interact with faculty. Attendance is required for problem-based learning sessions.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Hershey and University Park Campus
Our integrated four pillar curriculum model of biomedical sciences, clinical sciences, health humanities and health systems sciences utilizes problem based learning, simulation, small group and large group sessions, and patient-care experiences. Phase 1 provides integrated principles from all four pillars and starts a 17-month systems science component. Phase 2 includes clinical clerkships and electives integrating the four pillars. Phase 3 include acting internships, electives, and residency prep.

medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: The Penn State College of Medicine (PSCOM) has a strong commitment to training physicians who will practice primary care.  Primary care physicians play a crucial role in serving the health care needs of our communities by providing personalized, high quality, comprehensive, collaborative, and continuous care to individuals and their families.  This is especially important for our medically underserved communities. Three-year accelerated MD programs in Family Medicine, General Internal Medicine, and General Pediatrics were created to support student interest in primary care while reducing student debt and addressing the primary care physician shortage. We are committed to training future physicians to become advocates for health equity and excellence in health care for all.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: The Medical Student Research (MSR) program is an integral part of our curriculum. The program requires each student to participate in mentored health-related research. Students gain an understanding of the research process, limitations and variability of data, and application of research to clinical practice. Most students participate in multiple research projects during matriculation. Nearly 75% of students are an author on an article curated in Pubmed, and 40% of students were first authors on one or more manuscripts. The MSR program provides Penn State medical students with a distinct enhancement of their applications for residency and other post graduate programs. Research project topics include basic science, clinical research, translational research, precision medicine, global health, medical education, narrative and social medicine, systems research, epidemiology and population health. Opportunities to perform research occur throughout the curriculum.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
As Pennsylvania’s only rural academic medical center, we strive to improve our communities by addressing shortages, reducing disparities, and promoting inclusive policies.  Our vision is to be a world leader in the transformation of health care and in the enhancement of health for people everywhere.

Penn State College of Medicine has grown from one singular campus and a small class of medical students to a multi-campus academic, research and clinical care powerhouse and force for good. Since the first graduation in 1969, College of Medicine students have become productive physicians and scientists.

The College of Medicine was the first in the nation to have a dedicated Department of Humanities and a Department of Family and Community Medicine. 

College of Medicine and Medical Center faculty and physicians continue to integrate the latest biomedical knowledge and technology with compassionate care of patients, while educating the next generation of scientists and physicians.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Penn State College of Medicine and its academic partner, Penn State Health, are committed to enhancing the quality of life through improved health, the professional preparation of those who will serve the health needs of others and the discovery of knowledge that will benefit all. Our vision is to be a world leader in the transformation of health care and in the enhancement of health for people everywhere. 

We are committed to the education of medical and nursing students, basic science graduate students, medical residents and fellows, other students in healthcare related professions, and practicing health professionals. We seek to enroll students of exceptional quality, and their education will be based on the present and future health needs of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and the nation. Special recognition is given to the education of primary care providers.

Our objective is to provide a range of fully integrated patient care services for the people of central Pennsylvania and beyond. These services will extend from prevention of illness and maintenance of health through primary medical care to the highly sophisticated patient care expected at the nation’s premier academic medical centers.

We strive to be a national leader in pursuing scientific investigation and developing programs to advance medical and scientific knowledge, which will ultimately contribute to the health of the public, the practice of medicine, and the education of health professionals.

We will provide community outreach services to the public through health education, patient care, community activities, and applications of research. We endeavor to provide health education to the public. In turn, community support for our research missions fosters clinical applications that positively impact patient care.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Course Grades
Penn State College of Medicine recognizes that its applicants bring varied and rich undergraduate academic and personal experiences to their admissions credentials. We recognize that students most successful in our rigorous curriculum demonstrate excellence in coursework in the areas that strengthen their academic preparation.

Required academic courses (or the applicant’s institution’s equivalent) include:
•	General biology with lab (1 year/2 semesters)
•	General/inorganic chemistry with lab (1 year/2 semesters)
•	Organic chemistry with lab (1 year/2 semesters)
•	Physics with lab (1 year/2 semesters)
•	Biochemistry (1 semester)

Online coursework is generally not recommended. 

Courses that have Pass/Fail, Credit/No Credit, Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory as their grading are generally not recommended. However, consideration of this grading is given to coursework taken during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic (2020, 2021). It is recommended that applicants achieve a B- or higher in the required courses.


MCAT
The Admissions Committee will continue to require completion of the MCAT examination in order to apply to the College of Medicine. See Admissions Policies and Procedures on the Admissions website. 

The Penn State College of Medicine strictly adheres to the process and dates of the AMCAS Choose Your Medical School (CYMS) Tool as follows:

All accepted applicants are strongly encouraged to participate in the CYMS Tool starting in February and indicate “Plan to Enroll” if Penn State is a consideration for medical school.

After April 15 accepted applicants are required to hold no more than three acceptances. They may remain on other wait lists.

After April 30 Accepted applicants are required to participate in the Choose Your Medical school tool and adhere to the stated rules. 

Accepted applicants can hold only one acceptance and have the option of indicating “Plan to Enroll” or “Commit to Enroll”. A selection of “Commit to Enroll” indicates a final selection and applicants are expected to withdraw acceptance(s) from all other schools. 

An accepted applicant who selects “Plan to Enroll” must maintain one acceptance to Penn State, but can remain on other wait lists. Applicants who make a decision to matriculate to another medical school are expected to notify the Admissions Office within 24 hours by email.

At 21 days before matriculation, accepted applicants must select “Commit to Enroll” to remain in the entering class. Accepted applicants will be reminded of the deadline date by the Admissions Office. At this point accepted applicants are not allowed to accept offers from other medical schools or be considered for a waitlist position.

The AMCAS traffic rules are strictly enforced. The College of Medicine reserves the right to resend an offer of acceptance if improper activity is discovered.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Financial aid is granted based upon need as determined by federal methodology. Parental income information is required for university scholarship and loan consideration, as well as some other financial assistance programs.  The College of Medicine also has limited private, merit and need based scholarships available that are awarded to incoming and continuing students.  Secondary application fee waiver is granted if approved by AMCAS. The Financial Aid Office provides individualized financial aid counseling to all students every year that they are a federal loan borrower.  Additional financial aid information is available on the school's web site including the tuition and fees as set by the Board of Trustees in July each year. Work-Study stipends are available during the summer after first year medical school that supports medical student research projects.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Penn State College of Medicine accept applicants with good standing backgrounds who are, or will be, graduates of accredited colleges and universities in the U.S. or Canada before matriculation. There are no restrictions on the type of major a student selects who meets expectations in the designated required prerequisite areas. 

We recognize that our applicants bring varied and rich undergraduate academic and personal experiences to their admissions credentials. We also recognize that students most successful in our rigorous curriculum demonstrate excellence in coursework in the areas that strengthen their academic preparation. Because of this, specific coursework is now required for admission.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Applicants must demonstrate evidence of strong undergraduate or graduate achievement in both science and liberal arts areas.  Each class has students with majors in both science and non-science areas from a broad array of colleges and universities. The Committee has an interest in a record of service, variety of the student body, evidence of strong personal qualities, significant exposure to clinical settings, broad background experiences, leadership, unique activities, and competency in the four sections of the MCAT.  Each application is reviewed in a mission-aligned manner with balanced consideration of all AMCAS sections and responses to questions on the Penn State secondary application.  Applicants should be thoughtful in submitting letters of support from Pre-health committees when available and writers who know them well.  The Committee understands that some applicants will take non-traditional pathways to medical school.
